$comment: Surface manifest. 'default' = npm-package stdio (unfiltered). 'hosted-15' = the ORIGINAL, historical hosted default (pre-2026-07-20) — kept PINNED (do not resize) as a regression fixture for the eval harness (npm-package/eval/model-eval-runner.mjs --surface=hosted-15, npm-package/tests/eval/model-eval-runner.test.ts, .github/workflows/eval-harness.yml): it names the 15 tools that MUST stay routable by name even if one later moves off the live 'hosted' LISTING (see novada_browser below — pinned here on purpose, not stale). 'hosted' = the REAL, LIVE mcp.novada.com default LISTING as of 2026-10-14 (2026-07-20 core-derivation refactor, then Round 3's SHEIN empty-working-op-set exclusion and a 2026-10 connector-review pass that moved novada_browser into HOSTED_HIDDEN — see below), once hosted-server/vercel/api/mcp.ts's TOOLS array was changed from a hand-curated 15-tool literal to a derivation off npm-package/src/core.ts's `TOOLS` (the single source of truth; Round 4 made that derivation surface-aware — see mcp.ts's buildToolsForSurface) filtered by mcp.ts's `HOSTED_HIDDEN` set. This 'hosted' list is npm-package's 37 registered tools (`novada_scrape_shein` was removed entirely, not just hidden — zero working ops) minus HOSTED_HIDDEN's 9 exclusions (novada_browser_flow, novada_browser, novada_site_copy, novada_ip_whitelist, novada_static_ip_mgmt, novada_capture_apikey, novada_session_stats, novada_search_feedback, novada_verify — see mcp.ts's HOSTED_HIDDEN docstring for the rationale on each, including novada_browser's 2026-10 connector-review addition: every real browser action unconditionally fails on this runtime, so Directory review requires it be delisted). 'hosted-15' therefore intentionally contains ONE tool (novada_browser) no longer in 'hosted' — scripts/check-hosted-drift.mjs's gate (c) carries a documented, named exception for exactly this tool rather than requiring 'hosted-15' ⊆ 'hosted' unconditionally; any OTHER divergence still fails. scripts/check-hosted-drift.mjs verifies this list is (a) a subset of npm-package's REGISTERED_TOOL_NAMES, (b) an exact SET match against mcp.ts's live derived TOOLS output, (c) 'hosted-15' minus that one named exception is still a subset of 'hosted', and (d) that mcp.ts's TOOLS is actually derived from CORE_TOOLS (directly, or via Round 4's surface-rendered form) rather than a hand-curated literal (drift would otherwise be structurally impossible to reintroduce silently, per that script's docstring).
